question: Consider the following subjects under the Constitution of India: [Salient Features of Indian Constitution] I. List I-Union List, in the Seventh Schedule II. Extent of the executive power of a State III. Conditions of the Governor’s office For a constitutional amendment with respect to which of the above, ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States is required before presenting the bill to the President of India for assent?
rag_answer: According to Article 368 of the Constitution of India, any amendment that seeks to alter the provisions related to the Union List, the extent of the executive power of a State, and the conditions of the Governor’s office requires ratification by the Legislatures of not less than one-half of the States before being presented to the President for assent. Therefore, all three subjects mentioned (I, II, and III) fall under this requirement for ratification [Constitution of India, p. 260].

question: Consider the following pairs: [Fundamental Rights] Provision in the Constitution of India Stated under I. Separation of Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State The Directive Principles of the State Policy II. Valuing and preserving of the rich heritage of our composite culture The Fundamental Duties III. Prohibition of employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories The Fundamental Rights How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
rag_answer: Only one pair is correctly matched. The first pair, 'Separation of Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State', is a provision under the Directive Principles of State Policy, not Fundamental Rights. The second pair, 'Valuing and preserving of the rich heritage of our composite culture', is part of the Fundamental Duties, not Fundamental Rights. The third pair, 'Prohibition of employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories', is a Fundamental Right under Article 24. Therefore, only the third pair is correctly matched, making the correct option A (Only one). [Constitution of India, p. 37; NCERT Polity, p. 13]

question: Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India: [Union Executive] I. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review. II. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is correct because the exercise of the pardoning power by the President can indeed be subjected to limited judicial review, as established by the Supreme Court in various judgments. Statement II is incorrect because the President exercises this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers, as per Article 74 of the Constitution. Therefore, the correct option is A (I only) [Constitution of India, p. 63].

question: Consider the following statements: [Union Executive] I. If any question arises as to whether a Member of the House of the People has become subject to disqualification under the 10th Schedule, the President’s decision in accordance with the opinion of the Council of Union Ministers shall be final. II. There is no mention of the word ‘political party’ in the Constitution of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rag_answer: Both statements are incorrect. Statement I is incorrect because the President's decision regarding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is final for members of Parliament, not for members of the House of the People; it is the Governor's decision that is final for State Legislature members [Constitution of India, p. 117]. Statement II is also incorrect because the term 'political party' is indeed mentioned in the Constitution, specifically in the context of disqualifications under the Tenth Schedule [Constitution of India, p. 378]. Therefore, the correct option is D: Neither I nor II.

question: Consider the following statements: [Union Legislature] I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution. II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately. III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days’ notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution. Which of the statements given above are correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is correct as the Constitution states that the Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution [Constitution of India, p. 73]. Statement II is incorrect because the Constitution does not require a Member of the House of the People to resign from their political party upon being elected as Speaker. Statement III is correct as it mentions the procedure for the removal of the Speaker, which includes the requirement of a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, with at least fourteen days' notice [Constitution of India, p. 73]. Therefore, the correct option is C (I and III only).

question: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: [Union Legislature] I. An Ordinance can amend any Central Act. II. An Ordinance can abridge a Fundamental Right. III. An Ordinance can come into effect from a back date. Which of the statements given above are correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is correct because an Ordinance can amend any Central Act as per the provisions of the Constitution. Statement II is incorrect because an Ordinance cannot abridge a Fundamental Right, as it must conform to the Constitution. Statement III is also incorrect because an Ordinance cannot come into effect from a back date; it takes effect from the date of promulgation. Therefore, only statement I is correct, making the correct option A (I and II only) incorrect. The correct option is A.

question: Consider the following statements: [State Legislature & Executive] I. The Constitution of India/explicitly mentions that in certain spheres the Governor of a State acts in his/her own discretion. II. The President of India can, of his/her own, reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor of the State concerned. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is correct because the Constitution of India does mention that the Governor of a State can act in his/her own discretion in certain matters, as outlined in Article 163. However, Statement II is incorrect because the President cannot reserve a bill passed by a State Legislature for his/her consideration without it being forwarded by the Governor, as per Article 200. Therefore, the correct option is A (I only). [Constitution of India, p. 64]

question: With reference to the Indian polity, consider the following statements: [State Legislature & Executive] I. The Governor of a State is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his/her office. II. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted or continued against the Governor during his/her term of office. III. Members of a State Legislature are not liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said within the House. Which of the statements given above are correct?
rag_answer: All three statements are correct based on the Constitution of India. Statement I is correct because the Governor is not answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office [Constitution of India, p. 250]. Statement II is also correct as no criminal proceedings can be instituted or continued against the Governor during his term of office [Constitution of India, p. 250]. Lastly, Statement III is correct since members of a State Legislature are not liable to any proceedings in any court in respect of anything said within the House [Constitution of India, p. 250]. Therefore, the correct option is D: I, II and III.

question: Consider the following statements: [Local Government] I. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States. II. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years. III. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels and to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes and duties, leviable by the State, between the State and Panchayats at the intermediate level. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is incorrect because Panchayats at the intermediate level may not be constituted in a State having a population not exceeding twenty lakhs, meaning not all States have them [Constitution of India, p. 150]. Statement II is incorrect because the minimum age to be a member of a Panchayat is twenty-one years, not thirty [Constitution of India, p. 153]. Statement III is correct as the Chief Minister does constitute a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats [Constitution of India, p. 154]. Therefore, the statements that are not correct are I and II.

question: Consider the following pairs: [Local Government] State Description I. Arunachal Pradesh The capital is named after a fort, and the State has two National Parks II. rag_answer: Only one pair is correctly matched. I. Arunachal Pradesh is correctly described as having a capital named after a fort and having two National Parks. However, II. question: Consider the following statements: [Local Government] With reference to the Constitution of India, if an area in a State is declared as Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule I. the State Government loses its executive power in such areas and a local body assumes total administration II. the Union Government can take over the total administration of such areas under certain circumstances on the recommendations of the Governor Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
rag_answer: Statement I is incorrect because the State Government does not lose its executive power entirely in Scheduled Areas; rather, the administration is subject to certain provisions and the Governor's recommendations. Statement II is correct as the Union Government can take over the administration of Scheduled Areas under certain circumstances on the recommendations of the Governor, as outlined in the Constitution. Therefore, the correct option is B (II only). [Constitution of India, p. 164]

question: Consider the following activities: [Local Government] I. Production of crude oil-free II. Refining, storage and distribution of petroleum III. Marketing and sale of petroleum products IV. Production of natural gas How many of the above activities are regulated by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board in our country?
rag_answer: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board regulates the refining, storage, and distribution of petroleum (II) and the marketing and sale of petroleum products (III). However, it does not regulate the production of crude oil (I) or the production of natural gas (IV). Therefore, only two activities (II and III) are regulated by the Board, making the correct option B.
